# Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2005: The Real Alternative - Summary

The 2005 Liberal Democrat manifesto positions the party as Britain's genuine progressive alternative, built upon three foundational principles: Freedom, Fairness, and Trust.

## Economic and Fiscal Approach

The manifesto emphasises fiscal responsibility with fully costed proposals. The party pledges to maintain economic stability whilst making the tax system fairer. Their flagship fiscal policy proposes a 50% tax rate on income exceeding £100,000—affecting just 1% of taxpayers—to fund abolition of tuition fees, free elderly care, and Council Tax replacement. The manifesto argues that under Labour, the poorest 20% pay proportionally more tax than the richest 20%, which Liberal Democrats consider fundamentally unjust. Council Tax would be replaced with Local Income Tax based on ability to pay, saving typical households approximately £450 annually.

## Public Services

Healthcare policy focuses on freeing professionals from bureaucratic targets whilst delivering free personal care for elderly and disabled people. The party proposes faster diagnosis pathways, extended prescription charge exemptions, and smoking bans in enclosed public spaces.

Education priorities include abolishing all tuition and top-up fees, using Child Trust Fund savings to reduce class sizes to 20 in infant schools, and guaranteeing specialist teachers for core subjects. The party champions vocational training equality alongside academic pathways.

## Civil Liberties and Justice

The manifesto robustly opposes ID cards as expensive, illiberal, and ineffective, proposing instead to redirect funds toward 10,000 additional police officers. The party defended fundamental civil liberties against control orders and detention without trial, positioning themselves as defenders of democratic freedoms against government overreach. They support firm but fair asylum policies and a Single Equality Act outlawing all discrimination.

## Pensions and Social Security

Pension reform includes a "Citizen's Pension" based on residency rather than national insurance contributions, specifically addressing discrimination against women who interrupted careers for caring responsibilities. The manifesto promises £100+ monthly pension increases for over-75s and Winter Fuel Payments extended to severely disabled people.

## Environmental Commitments

Environmental policy runs as a "green thread" throughout, reflecting the party's self-identification as Britain's greenest mainstream party. Commitments include 20% renewable electricity by 2020, opposing nuclear power replacement, promoting cleaner transport, zero municipal waste goals, and international climate leadership through "contraction and convergence" principles.

## International Affairs

The manifesto strongly condemns the Iraq War as illegal, costly, and based on flawed intelligence, whilst acknowledging moral obligations to support Iraqi reconstruction. European engagement is championed, with support for EU constitution ratification via referendum and eventual euro membership subject to appropriate economic conditions. Aid spending should reach 0.7% of GNI by 2011.

## Constitutional Reform

Proposals include curbing Prime Ministerial power, introducing STV voting for genuine proportional representation, creating a predominantly elected second chamber, strengthening local democracy, and devolving powers from Whitehall. The manifesto argues successive governments have dangerously concentrated power whilst undermining local communities.

## Rural Communities

The party promises fair food prices through trade fairness legislation, CAP reform supporting family farms, fisheries policy reform, and enhanced animal welfare through an Animal Protection Commission.

The manifesto concludes with ten contrasts against Labour/Conservative positions, positioning Liberal Democrats as the party of principle, fairness, and genuine opposition to establishment politics.
